title: Health insurance for expatriates
excerpt: Preparing an assessment when relocating to Moldova or abroad: actual residence, duration, services, payment, family and confidentiality.

seo.title: Expatriate health insurance in Moldova: what to check | ING Broker
seo.description: Separate travel from long-term residence and mandatory status from a private programme. Check people, countries, services and records without residence-permit promises.
seo.keywords: expat health insurance Moldova, foreign residents health insurance, relocation medical programme, long term residence insurance, expatriate medical cover

author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
For someone living or working in another country, the question is not only whether they have medical insurance but where they actually live, for how long and which services they need. Short-trip insurance is not the same as a long-stay programme. For a foreign resident in Moldova, start with local circumstances and applicable documents.

This article explains administrative preparation for expatriate insurance assessment. It confirms neither acceptance of an individual nor suitability as evidence for a residence permit. It also confirms no international insurance offer through ING Broker. Check those separately in current product documents and with the institution requesting evidence.

Two situations that should not be mixed

A foreign citizen moving to Chișinău has different questions from a Moldovan going abroad to work. The first situation concerns access in Moldova and status in its local system. The second concerns the destination, duration and requirements abroad. This page does not establish those foreign requirements.

Record citizenship, the country of actual residence, the country where medical help is sought and the purpose of the stay. Do not publish identity documents for a general answer. A description without identifiers can establish which information and channel are needed next.

Assess family members individually. An employee, partner and child are not automatically included together. Ask for people, periods and joining arrangements rather than a general “family protection” statement.

Consider a hypothetical Moldovan employer welcoming a foreign specialist and family. Start with purpose, countries and periods, not a full medical archive. Review each person separately; one employer request does not establish identical eligibility or acceptance of every certificate.

Mandatory insurance and private programmes

In Moldova, check mandatory health insurance status through CNAM. A private card, paid consultation or employer name does not determine it. Use official channels and avoid entering personal information on unconfirmed pages.

A voluntary programme requires separate review of accepted people, services, institutions and access. Do not present it as an automatic substitute for legal requirements, especially when evidence is requested by employers, schools or authorities.

Ask exactly which document is required and who determines acceptance. A translated commercial certificate does not, by itself, confirm that all the requesting institution's conditions have been met. Keep written requirements and competent answers rather than an undocumented conversation.

Travel or residence: why duration matters

A journey has a declared period and purpose. Moving for work, study or family may involve repeated needs rather than only an unforeseen incident during a visit. Describe reality before comparing prices and ask whether the product can assess it.

Clarify departure, contract commencement and whether the person is already abroad. Online purchase does not automatically cover an already started situation. Read the commencement and eligibility provisions in the document applicable to that person and programme.

For work across countries, describe recurring journeys and the main place of residence. A territory list alone does not explain residence, temporary visits and home returns. Request answers for each actual situation.

Separate residence, temporary journeys and returns, with confirmed and pending statuses. Do not transfer short-visit conditions to long-term work by name. Preserve the receiving institution's actual evidence requirement. For services, ask categories, location, access, approval and payment without selecting treatment from marketing.

Which services are assessed?

Separate planned consultations, investigations, hospitalisation and unforeseen assistance. General wording about medical services does not establish that every category is included. The checklist concerns administrative access and contract questions, not recommendations for medical treatment.

For each category, ask about network, referrals, approval and payment. A particular town may matter, not only a country. Do not assume a national presentation means identical access in every smaller locality.

Ask about document language, assistance language and required invoice or report translations. Do not promise translation or coordination in every language unless confirmed by the programme.

Direct payment and reimbursement

Direct payment involves an arrangement between programme and provider. Reimbursement may mean paying initially and requesting later assessment. A clinic on a partner list does not establish either mechanism for every service.

Where advance payment is needed, ask which records to retain, assessment currency and how decisions are communicated. These affect personal budgeting. A large limit does not mean no temporary personal payment.

Distinguish a confirmed appointment from financial acceptance. They may be separate steps. Keep written answers and reference numbers without publishing them alongside medical details.

Health information and confidentiality

Do not send full medical histories through general contact forms. First clarify information, recipient and purpose. Answer an applicable questionnaire accurately through the indicated channel without deliberate omission or unsolicited extra detail.

An employer may coordinate administration without needing every medical record. Separate enrolment from medical or financial assessment. Clarify who can communicate for another family member.

Discuss known conditions, planned investigations and recurring care under the actual document. Do not assume acceptance or make medical decisions from insurance copy. Doctors and insurers have different roles.

Keep versions controlled so another authorised colleague can identify dates and unresolved questions. This supports accurate communication without certifying mandatory status, residence permits or entitlement to a particular medical payment.

Preparing relocation or an employer change

Create a timeline for old programme ending, new contract starting, travel and transition. Check every person, not only the employee. Leaving the administrative review until after arrival can leave gaps or unresolved questions.

Keep assistance contacts and documents accessible, including offline. Clarify planned services early. Do not delay appropriate emergency medical help to read an article or compare offers.

At renewal, ask about network, limits and conditions. An unchanged product name does not mean identical clauses. Read new wording before assuming continuity of a service.

Check transition dates from real records and keep a prepared list distinct from issued confirmation. Payment initiation does not establish active protection. Retain source, date and applicable version for answers, and separate staff guidance from personal assessment. This example is not an actual customer, immigration advice or an international policy offer.

A useful comparison record

For each programme, record accepted residence, eligible people, territories, services and network. Add the payment mechanism, approval procedure and documents needed for reimbursement. Mark gaps unconfirmed rather than filling them from advertising impressions.

A Moldovan employer receiving a foreign specialist can use this before requesting personal documents. Clarify circumstances and requirements first, then collect only necessary information. This is organisation, not confirmation of an ING Broker expatriate product.

Review actual countries and periods through the company's appropriate process without collecting unnecessary private itineraries. If circumstances change, ask about applicable conditions rather than relying on an unchanged programme name.

Temporary returns and visits elsewhere

A person resident abroad may return home, while a foreign resident of Moldova may travel briefly. Separate residence and temporary travel. A residence-country clause does not necessarily operate identically during visits. Request written boundaries for actual circumstances.

Ask about services starting in one country before returning to another. This is an administrative scenario, not advice to travel for care. Medical care and ability to travel require competent advice; insurance documents separately address territories and services.

A relocation country-and-period record need not include private addresses or medical files. Additional personal information should be requested only after the procedure and appropriate recipient are identified. It should not be attached by default to every administrative email.

At relocation end, clarify programme termination and records needed for earlier-period claims. A general article cannot determine whether a particular right is retained or lost when the programme ends. Identify contract, version and chronology first.

For an internal check, use a fictional temporary journey from the actual residence country. Record the dates and question to clarify, without deciding whether medical treatment or travel is appropriate. Check whether one old answer has been reused for family members with different periods. Do not add diagnoses and identity copies merely to fill a table. Agree recipient and scope before extra information. A document requested for an administrative purpose needs checking separately from clinic availability and payment arrangements. A clear file prevents confusion but guarantees neither institutional acceptance nor access to every service or an insurer's decision.

Frequently asked questions about expatriates

Is travel insurance enough for long-term work?

A name alone cannot establish that. Check duration, purpose, residence and eligibility. Requirements of the institution asking for evidence need separate confirmation.

Should foreigners in Moldova check CNAM status?

Yes, check the mandatory system through relevant official channels. A private programme alone confirms neither AOAM status nor individual requirements.

Are all countries and clinics included?

Do not assume so. Request territory, network and outside-network rules, including payment. A commercial map does not replace conditions.

What can I send initially?

Countries, period, purpose and number of people. Identity and medical information should be supplied later only where necessary and through the agreed channel. This is information, not a confirmed offer.

Next step

Request a discussion with ING Broker to check assessment and brokering possibilities. The broker explains options and acts as intermediary. Risk acceptance, conditions and claims decisions belong to the insurer under the contract. This guide does not confirm product availability or cover for an individual case.
